why: One level, R 16, origin 0, voxel 0.25 m, valid range [0.375, 3.625] m on each axis (local [1.5, 14.5] voxels). Texels are filled analytically from the plane z 2.125 m: a = |z_centre - 2.125| metres, rgb 0. Texel centres sit at 0.25 k + 0.125 m, and k = 8 gives the centre 2.125 m exactly, so the plane lies on a layer of voxel centres. The texel values are a = 0.25 |k - 8|; a trilinear sample at z between two centres is the linear interpolation of those values, which on each side of the plane is exactly |z - 2.125| (h = |z - 2.125|, with no flat segment). So within the valid range the sample is h = |z - 2.125| at every point. Each ray is walked by the contract's rules: t from start, step clamp(h, 0.5 voxel, 4 voxel); only an approaching sample (the first of its level, or h below the previous sample of the same level) darkens; y = h^2 / (2 ph) when ph < 1e19 and h < 2 ph, dd = sqrt(max(h^2 - y^2, 0)) - 0.5 voxel, radius = max(tan_half max(t - y, 1e-4), 0.5 voxel), res = min(res, dd / radius); the walk stops when res < -1; the final value is max(res, -1) followed by Quilez's 0.25 (1 + res)^2 (2 - res). There is no hard cut and no voxel fade. max_steps is 32 throughout.

cases.name: parallel to the plane
cases.why: Inputs unchanged; the plane moved from 2.0 to 2.125, so the derived h changes from 0.75 to 0.875. The ray stays at y 2.0 and z 1.25, inside the valid range, so level_at returns 0 for every sample, and h = |1.25 - 2.125| = 0.875 for every x. Sample 1 (t 0.25, x 1.25, ph 1e20): approaching; y = 0 because ph is not below 1e19; dd = 0.875 - 0.125 = 0.75; radius = max(0.5 x 0.25, 0.125) = 0.125; res = min(1, 6) = 1. Then ph = 0.875 and the step is clamp(0.875, 0.125, 1.0) = 0.875, so t = 1.125 (x 2.125, inside the range). Sample 2: h = 0.875 equals ph, so it is not approaching and never darkens. The step of 0.875 takes t to 2.0, beyond max_t 1.5, so the loop ends. res = 1 and 0.25 x 4 x 1 = 1.

cases.name: toward the plane, crossing
cases.why: Hand walk along +z, z = 0.5 + t, x = 2.0 and y = 2.0 (local 8 voxels; every sample z lies in [0.75, 2.125], inside the range [0.375, 3.625], so level 0 holds throughout). Sample 1 (t 0.25, z 0.75): h = |0.75 - 2.125| = 1.375; ph is 1e20, so it is approaching, y = 0, dd = 1.375 - 0.125 = 1.25 and radius = max(0.5 x 0.25, 0.125) = 0.125, so res = min(1, 10) = 1. Step clamp(1.375, 0.125, 1.0) = 1.0, so t = 1.25. Sample 2 (t 1.25, z 1.75): h = 0.375 < ph = 1.375, so approaching; y = 0.140625 / 2.75 = 0.051136; sqrt(h^2 - y^2) = 0.371497; dd = 0.371497 - 0.125 = 0.246497; radius = max(0.5 x (1.25 - 0.051136), 0.125) = 0.599432; res = 0.411218. Step clamp(0.375, 0.125, 1.0) = 0.375, so t = 1.625. Sample 3 (t 1.625, z 2.125): the texel centre on the plane gives h = 0 exactly (trilinear weight 0 on a = 0). h < ph = 0.375, so approaching; y = 0, dd = 0 - 0.125 = -0.125 and radius = max(0.5 x 1.625, 0.125) = 0.8125, so res = min(0.411218, -0.153846) = -0.153846. The walk continues because res is not below -1: t 1.75 (h 0.375, not approaching), 2.125 (h 0, radius 1.0625, ratio -0.117647, above the current res), 2.25, 2.375 and 2.625, then 3.125, beyond max_t 3.0. No later sample lowers res, so res = -0.153846 = -2/13 and 0.25 x (11/13)^2 x (28/13) = 0.385526. A crossing darkens without a hard cut; it reaches 0 only when dd <= -radius.

cases.name: empty volume
cases.why: No level: level_at returns levels.len() = 0 at the first sample, the walk breaks before any sample, res stays 1 and 0.25 x 4 x 1 = 1.
